_comment: Soil, the surface a cell is made of. A type (data/terrain/terrain_types.json) says what ground DOES - how fast it is crossed, whether it can be crossed, how much it blocks sight. A soil says what ground IS MADE OF - what it dries to, what it churns into when it is wet, which detail overlay the renderer paints on it, and a small movement modifier of its own. The two are independent on purpose: a wood (type) can stand on gravel (soil), and a bog is a soil and a wetness, not a fifth kind of terrain. A cell's final movement multiplier is composed from its type, its soil, its vegetation, its wetness and its slope once, at generation time, and cached - see BattlefieldTerrain._resolve_move().

_fields.id: stable key, written into the per-cell soil array
_fields.name: what a player would call it
_fields.move_modifier: multiplied onto the type's multiplier; keep these close to 1.0 so a soil seasons the ground rather than re-writing the rule
_fields.moisture: 0..1, what this soil is like when wet - the generator prefers soils whose moisture matches the cell's
_fields.overlay: the detail overlay this soil wears by default (see the biome's overlays list)

soils.name: Grass
soils.description: The default ground of a green country.

soils.name: Bare dirt
soils.description: Where the turf is gone - worn tracks, camps, the ground around a village.

soils.name: Mud
soils.description: Dirt holding water. Heavy to walk on and worse to charge over.

soils.name: River silt
soils.description: The soft, pale ground a river leaves when it has been somewhere and gone.

soils.name: Sand
soils.description: Loose and bright. Easy enough to cross, hard to hold a line on.

soils.name: Gravel
soils.description: Loose stone. Footing is uncertain but the ground drains.

soils.name: Bare rock
soils.description: Bedrock at the surface. Nothing grows here and nothing digs in.

soils.name: Snow
soils.description: Old snow, packed enough to walk on and deep enough to slow the step.
